mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.15%) signals an accommodative monetary policy environment that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains at or below 0.15% for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 9.5%) indicates a weak labor market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 9.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST < 580) and retail sales (RSAFS < 350000) signals a weakening consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 580 and RSAFS < 350000, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 9.0%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals weak economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 9.0%, INDPRO < 100, and S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO shows a sustained upward trend (3-month consecutive increases) but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST < 580) signals weak residential construction and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 580, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 215 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains at or below 0.15%, the market perceives the Federal Reserve as being behind the curve, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 215 and FEDFUNDS <= 0.15%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A weak labor market (PAYEMS < 129000) indicates slowing job growth and potential economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS < 129000, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
